body: Multimodal Large Language Models face significant efficiency challenges that stem from two distinct yet coupled sources: data redundancy and computational redundancy. While most methods focus on data redundancy by pruning visual tokens from the output of the visual encoder or computing redundancy in LLM decoders using blockwise importance, the finer-grained inter-layer representation shifts and the distribution differences within the layers themselves have not been fully explored. In this work, we comprehensively investigate this dual-level inefficiency. We posit that intermediate layer tokens from vision encoders should be considered for effective visual token pruning, as semantic focus shifts across layers, with middle-layer tokens capturing more detailed object-centric information that deeper layers may abstract away. Furthermore, we reveal the differential contributions of Attention and FFNs across distinct LLM decoder layers. Building upon these discoveries, we propose SPIDER, a training-free framework that integrates multi-layer Semantic visual token PrunIng with an aDaptive sub-layER skipping mechanism. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that SPIDER consistently maintains strong performance across various MLLM architectures and reduction ratios. For instance, on LLaVA-NeXT-7B, SPIDER reduces FLOPs by 79% while maintaining 96% of the baseline performance.
summaryZh: 针对多模态大模型（MLLM）在视觉与计算上的双重冗余问题，本文提出了SPIDER框架。该方法通过分析视觉编码器中间层语义信息的分布差异，实现了多层语义视觉Token剪枝，并结合自适应子层跳过机制，针对性地优化了注意力机制与前馈网络（FFN）的计算贡献。实验证明，SPIDER在无需训练的情况下，在LLaVA-NeXT-7B模型上实现了79%的FLOPs降低，同时保持了96%的原始性能，为边缘侧多模态模型部署提供了高效的优化方案。

glossary.explanationZh: 多模态大模型，指能够处理视觉、文本等多种输入数据的模型。
Token剪枝，指通过移除冗余的视觉Token来减少计算量。
浮点运算次数，衡量模型计算复杂度的指标。
注意力机制，Transformer模型的核心组件。
前馈神经网络，Transformer层中的关键计算模块。
